```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# the code of the benchmark is in scripts in the directory code (one to
# prepare the data, one to run the programs from the command line, with the
# scripts it runs for gt_radmix() and OpenADMIXTURE.jl, and one to run
# gt_radmix() in an R session), from which the chunks below are read
# (purl = FALSE because pkgdown purls this file from the package root when
# looking for images, where these relative paths do not exist)
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_data.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_radmix_cli.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_openadmixture.jl")
knitr::read_chunk("code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R")
# the directory with the results of the benchmark (data/admixture_benchmark,
# or data/admixture_benchmark_quick for the results of a quick run)
results_dir <- params$results_dir
```

> **Note:** the results shown in this article are, for now, those of a
> small subset of the data (see [The data](#the-data)), run on a laptop
> with 4 cores, to check the benchmark. They will be replaced by those of
> the full benchmark.

`gt_radmix()` estimates ancestry proportions with the method of ADMIXTURE
(Alexander et al. 2009), directly from the backing file of a `gen_tibble`.
It uses a modified version of the algorithm of OpenADMIXTURE (Ko et al.
2023), whose C++ code is largely ported from OpenADMIXTURE.jl, and we
implemented the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE, which is not part of
OpenADMIXTURE. This article compares it with three programs that fit the
same model: ADMIXTURE itself, fastmixture (Santander et al. 2024), and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl, the Julia implementation of OpenADMIXTURE (without its
selection of ancestry informative markers). The comparison uses the Human
Genome Diversity Project (HGDP). It checks that the programs find the same
ancestry proportions, and measures how long each takes on different
numbers of cores, with and without cross-validation (which OpenADMIXTURE.jl
does not have).

All the programs are timed from the command line, each run being a new
process that starts the program, reads the data and saves the results.
`gt_radmix()` is also timed in an R session, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl in a
Julia session, in which the package is already loaded (see
[How long do they take?](#how-long-do-they-take)).

The [results](#results) come first. The second part,
[How the benchmark was run](#how-the-benchmark-was-run), describes the data
and the runs, with their code, and how to run the benchmark again.

# Results


```{r read_results, include = FALSE}
# each program, and how it is run (from the command line, or in an R or
# Julia session), in the order of the tables and plots
tool_labels <- c(
  radmix_cli = "gt_radmix() (command line)",
  radmix = "gt_radmix() (R session)",
  admixture = "ADMIXTURE",
  fastmixture = "fastmixture",
  openadmixture_cli = "OpenADMIXTURE.jl (command line)",
  openadmixture = "OpenADMIXTURE.jl (Julia session)"
)
# the program of each of them
tool_program <- c(
  radmix_cli = "radmix", radmix = "radmix", admixture = "admixture",
  fastmixture = "fastmixture", openadmixture_cli = "openadmixture",
  openadmixture = "openadmixture"
)
program_labels <- c(
  radmix = "gt_radmix()",
  admixture = "ADMIXTURE",
  fastmixture = "fastmixture",
  openadmixture = "OpenADMIXTURE.jl"
)
# one row per run, with its time, log-likelihood, cross-validation error
# and number of iterations, and the name of the files of its Q matrix and
# log (e.g. admixture_t4_cv for ADMIXTURE on 4 cores with cross-validation)
timings <- bind_rows(
  read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "timings_cli.csv")),
  read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "timings_radmix.csv"))
) %>%
  mutate(

  )

session_r <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "session_r.csv"))
session_value <- function(session, item) session$value[session$item == item]
n_indiv <- as.integer(session_value(session_cli, "individuals"))
# the numbers of cores, e.g. "1, 2 and 4"
cores_text <- knitr::combine_words(
  sort(unique(timings$n_cores)),
  oxford_comma = FALSE
)

# the population and region of the individual of each row of the Q matrices
individuals <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "individuals.csv"))
```

```{r align_q, include = FALSE}
# the Q matrix of a run
read_q <- function(run) {
  as.matrix(read.table(file.path(results_dir, "Q", paste0(run, ".Q"))))
}
# all the permutations of 1:n, one per row
permutations <- function(n) {
  if (n == 1) {
    return(matrix(1L))
  }
  smaller <- permutations(n - 1)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(first) {
    others <- setdiff(seq_len(n), first)
    cbind(first, matrix(others[smaller], ncol = n - 1))
  }))
}
# the clusters of different runs are numbered arbitrarily, so the columns of
# a Q matrix are reordered to best match those of a reference (with the
# smallest sum of squared differences, trying all the permutations)
align_q <- function(q, reference) {
  perms <- permutations(ncol(q))
  ssd <- apply(perms, 1, function(perm) sum((q[, perm] - reference)^2))
  unname(q[, perms[which.min(ssd), ]])
}
```

```{r agreement, include = FALSE}
# the reference: ADMIXTURE on the fewest cores, without cross-validation
min_cores <- min(timings$n_cores)
max_cores <- max(timings$n_cores)
reference_run <- paste0("admixture_t", min_cores, "_nocv")
q_ref <- read_q(reference_run)
k <- ncol(q_ref)
# the Q matrix of each run, with its clusters in the order of the reference
q_aligned <- lapply(
  setNames(timings$run, timings$run),
  function(run) align_q(read_q(run), q_ref)
)
max_diff <- function(a, b) max(abs(a - b))
rmse <- function(a, b) sqrt(mean((a - b)^2))
# for each run, the difference in log-likelihood from the reference, the
# largest difference in the ancestry proportions from the run of the same
# program on the fewest cores without cross-validation, and the RMSE and
# largest difference from the reference
agreement <- timings %>%
  mutate(
    own_run = paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv"),
    loglik_diff = loglik - loglik[run == reference_run],
    diff_own = mapply(
      function(run, own_run) max_diff(q_aligned[[run]], q_aligned[[own_run]]),
      run, own_run
    ),
    rmse_ref = vapply(run, function(r) rmse(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0),
    diff_ref = vapply(run, function(r) max_diff(q_aligned[[r]], q_ref), 0)
  )
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers for the text: the time of a run, the agreement of a program with
# ADMIXTURE (on the fewest cores, without cross-validation), and the largest
# difference between the runs of a program
time_of <- function(tool, n_cores = min_cores, crossval = FALSE) {
  timings$seconds[
    timings$tool == tool & timings$n_cores == n_cores &
      timings$crossval == crossval
  ]
}
format_seconds <- function(x) {
  formatC(signif(x, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3, big.mark = ",")
}
format_diff <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x == 0, "0", formatC(signif(x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2))
}
agreement_of <- function(tool, column) {
  agreement[[column]][agreement$run == paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]
}
runs_differ_by <- function(tool) {
  diff <- max(agreement$diff_own[agreement$tool == tool])
  if (diff == 0) {
    "identical ancestry proportions"
  } else {
    paste("ancestry proportions that differ by up to", format_diff(diff))
  }
}
# the time taken to start R and load tidygenclust, and to start Julia, load
# OpenADMIXTURE.jl and compile its code: the median difference between the
# runs from the command line and in a session (with the same settings)
startup_of <- function(program) {
  runs <- timings[tool_program[as.character(timings$tool)] == program, ]
  cli <- runs[grepl("_cli$", runs$tool), ]
  session <- runs[!grepl("_cli$", runs$tool), ]
  setting <- function(x) paste(x$n_cores, x$crossval)
  session_seconds <- session$seconds[match(setting(cli), setting(session))]
  median(cli$seconds - session_seconds, na.rm = TRUE)
}
# the runs that ended at a lower log-likelihood than ADMIXTURE (by more than
# 1), and so at another local optimum
local_optima <- agreement %>%
  filter(loglik_diff < -1) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      tool_labels[as.character(tool)], " on ", n_cores,
      if_else(n_cores == 1, " core", " cores"),
      if_else(crossval, " with cross-validation", "")
    )
  )
local_optima_text <- if (nrow(local_optima) == 0) {
  paste(
    "Here, all the runs reached the log-likelihood of ADMIXTURE, to within",
    "1."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "Here, this happened to ", nrow(local_optima),
    if_else(nrow(local_optima) == 1, " run", " runs"), " (",
    paste(local_optima$label, collapse = "; "),
    "), whose log-likelihood is lower than that of ADMIXTURE by up to ",
    format_diff(max(-local_optima$loglik_diff)), "."
  )
}
```

## Summary

The four programs estimated the ancestry proportions of `r n_indiv`
individuals of the HGDP, typed at `r format(n_loci, big.mark = ",")` loci,
for K = `r k` ancestral populations (see [The data](#the-data)):

- From the command line, on `r min_cores` core, without cross-validation,
  `gt_radmix()` took `r format_seconds(time_of("radmix_cli"))` s,
  ADMIXTURE `r format_seconds(time_of("admixture"))` s, fastmixture
  `r format_seconds(time_of("fastmixture"))` s and OpenADMIXTURE.jl
  `r format_seconds(time_of("openadmixture_cli"))` s; on `r max_cores`
  cores, they took `r format_seconds(time_of("radmix_cli", max_cores))` s,
  `r format_seconds(time_of("admixture", max_cores))` s,
  `r format_seconds(time_of("fastmixture", max_cores))` s and
  `r format_seconds(time_of("openadmixture_cli", max_cores))` s.
- Starting R and loading `tidygenclust` took about
  `r format_seconds(startup_of("radmix"))` s of the time of `gt_radmix()`
  from the command line. Starting Julia, loading OpenADMIXTURE.jl and
  compiling its code took about
  `r format_seconds(startup_of("openadmixture"))` s: in a Julia session in
  which OpenADMIXTURE.jl has already been used, its fit took
  `r format_seconds(time_of("openadmixture"))` s on `r min_cores` core.
- Compared with ADMIXTURE (on `r min_cores` core, without
  cross-validation), the log-likelihood of `gt_radmix()` differs by
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("radmix", "loglik_diff"))`, that of
  fastmixture by `r format_diff(agreement_of("fastmixture", "loglik_diff"))`,
  and that of OpenADMIXTURE.jl by
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("openadmixture", "loglik_diff"))`. Their
  ancestry proportions differ from those of ADMIXTURE by up to
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("radmix", "diff_ref"))`,
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("fastmixture", "diff_ref"))` and
  `r format_diff(agreement_of("openadmixture", "diff_ref"))` respectively.
- Across numbers of cores, with and without cross-validation,
  `gt_radmix()` gives `r runs_differ_by("radmix")`, ADMIXTURE
  `r runs_differ_by("admixture")`, fastmixture
  `r runs_differ_by("fastmixture")`, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl (without
  cross-validation) `r runs_differ_by("openadmixture")`.

## Do the programs find the same ancestry proportions?

All the programs maximise the same likelihood, but each starts from its
own random values and stops according to its own convergence criterion.
Each run is compared with ADMIXTURE on `r min_cores` core without
cross-validation, after matching its clusters to those of ADMIXTURE:

```{r table_agreement, echo = FALSE}
agreement %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores, crossval) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    crossval = if_else(crossval, "yes", "no"),
    loglik = formatC(loglik, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","),
    across(c(loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref), format_diff)
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, crossval, loglik, loglik_diff, diff_own, rmse_ref, diff_ref
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "CV", "Log-likelihood", "Difference",
      "Largest difference (same program)", "RMSE (ADMIXTURE)",
      "Largest difference (ADMIXTURE)"
    ),
    align = "lllrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Log-likelihood of each run (fastmixture reports it with one decimal), ",
      "and its difference from that of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core ",
      "without cross-validation (CV; positive when higher). ",
      "Largest absolute difference between the ancestry proportions of each ",
      "run and those of the same program on ", min_cores, " core without ",
      "CV, and root mean square error (RMSE) and largest absolute difference ",
      "from those of ADMIXTURE on ", min_cores, " core without CV. The Q ",
      "matrices are stored with 6 decimals, so differences smaller than ",
      "1e-6 do not show."
    )
  )
```

Each program was run once for each number of cores, from a single random
start (with seed 1, but each program draws its own random values), so a
run can end at another local optimum of the likelihood, with a lower
log-likelihood and different ancestry proportions.
`r local_optima_text`

The ancestry proportions from each program (on `r min_cores` core, without
cross-validation, and in a session for `gt_radmix()` and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl), with the individuals grouped by region and population:

```{r plot_q, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
# the regions of the HGDP, from west to east
region_levels <- c(
  "Africa", "Middle_East", "Europe", "Central_South_Asia", "East_Asia",
  "Oceania", "America"
)
# the individuals are ordered by region and population, and, within each
# population, by the ancestry (in the reference) from its main cluster
main_cluster <- vapply(
  split(seq_len(nrow(q_ref)), individuals$population),
  function(rows) which.max(colMeans(q_ref[rows, , drop = FALSE])),
  integer(1)
)
main_ancestry <- q_ref[cbind(
  seq_len(nrow(q_ref)),
  main_cluster[individuals$population]
)]
indiv_order <- order(
  factor(individuals$region, region_levels),
  individuals$population,
  -main_ancestry
)
q_long <- bind_rows(lapply(names(program_labels), function(tool) {
  q <- q_aligned[[paste0(tool, "_t", min_cores, "_nocv")]][indiv_order, ]
  data.frame(
    tool = tool,
    individual = rep(seq_len(nrow(q)), k),
    region = rep(individuals$region[indiv_order], k),
    cluster = factor(rep(seq_len(k), each = nrow(q))),
    proportion = as.vector(q)
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = factor(tool, names(program_labels)),
    region = factor(region, region_levels)
  )
# one colour per cluster (from the Okabe-Ito palette)
cluster_colours <- c(
  "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00",
  "#CC79A7", "#999999"
)
ggplot(q_long, aes(x = individual, y = proportion, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  facet_grid(
    tool ~ region,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    labeller = labeller(
      tool = program_labels,
      region = function(x) gsub("_", " ", x)
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.1, "lines"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)
  )
```

## How long do they take?

The times of ADMIXTURE and fastmixture are those of runs from the command
line: each run is a new process, which starts the program, reads the bed
file and writes the estimates of Q and P to text files. `gt_radmix()` and
OpenADMIXTURE.jl are timed in the same way, with `Rscript` and `julia`
(command line), and also in a session, where R or Julia is already running
with the package loaded:

- for `gt_radmix()`, the time of reading the bed file into a `gen_tibble`
  (and its backing file), running `gt_radmix()`, and saving the resulting
  `gt_admix` object, with Q and P, to an RDS file. In an analysis with
  several values of K, or several runs, the `gen_tibble` would only be read
  once;
- for OpenADMIXTURE.jl, the time of its fit (including reading the bed file
  and writing Q and P), measured in Julia after a first, untimed run on a
  small subset of the data. Julia compiles the code of a function the first
  time it is called, so this is the time of a fit in a Julia session in
  which OpenADMIXTURE.jl has already been used.

```{r plot_timings, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# one colour per program, and one type of line per way of running it
program_colours <- c(
  radmix = "#2a78d6",
  admixture = "#eb6834",
  fastmixture = "#1baf7a",
  openadmixture = "#eda100"
)
setting_labels <- c(
  cli = "Command line",
  session = "Session (R or Julia)"
)
timings %>%
  mutate(
    program = factor(tool_program[as.character(tool)], names(program_labels)),
    setting = factor(
      if_else(tool %in% c("radmix", "openadmixture"), "session", "cli"),
      names(setting_labels)
    ),
    crossval = if_else(
      crossval,
      "With cross-validation",
      "Without cross-validation"
    ),
    crossval = factor(
      crossval,
      c("Without cross-validation", "With cross-validation")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = n_cores, y = seconds, colour = program, linetype = setting,
    group = tool
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~crossval) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(timings$n_cores))) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = program_colours, labels = program_labels) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(cli = "solid", session = "22"),
    labels = setting_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Cores", y = "Time (s, log scale)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )
```

```{r table_timings, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  group_by(tool, crossval) %>%
  mutate(speed_up = seconds[n_cores == min_cores] / seconds) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, crossval, seconds, speed_up) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = crossval, values_from = c(seconds, speed_up)) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    across(
      starts_with("seconds"),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "-", format_seconds(.x))
    ),
    across(
      starts_with("speed_up"),
      ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "-", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 1))
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    tool, n_cores, seconds_FALSE, speed_up_FALSE, seconds_TRUE, speed_up_TRUE
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program", "Cores", "Time (s)", "Speed-up", "Time with CV (s)",
      "Speed-up with CV"
    ),
    align = "lrrrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Time (s) taken by each run, without and with cross-validation (CV), ",
      "and speed-up relative to the run of the same program on ", min_cores,
      " core. OpenADMIXTURE.jl has no cross-validation."
    )
  )
```

Starting R and loading `tidygenclust` adds about
`r format_seconds(startup_of("radmix"))` s to each run of `gt_radmix()`
from the command line. Starting Julia, loading OpenADMIXTURE.jl and
compiling its code adds about
`r format_seconds(startup_of("openadmixture"))` s to each run of
OpenADMIXTURE.jl (these are the median differences between the runs from
the command line and in a session).

## Cross-validation errors

```{r table_cv, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  filter(crossval) %>%
  arrange(tool, n_cores) %>%
  mutate(
    tool = tool_labels[as.character(tool)],
    cv_error = formatC(cv_error, format = "f", digits = 5)
  ) %>%
  select(tool, n_cores, cv_error) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_cores, values_from = cv_error) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Program",
      paste(
        sort(unique(timings$n_cores)),
        if_else(sort(unique(timings$n_cores)) == 1, "core", "cores")
      )
    ),
    align = "lrrr",
    caption = "Cross-validation error of each program, on each number of cores."
  )
```

OpenADMIXTURE.jl has no cross-validation: we implemented in `gt_radmix()`
that of ADMIXTURE. ADMIXTURE and `gt_radmix()` compute the same
cross-validation error (Alexander and Lange 2011): they hold out a fold of
the genotypes, refit the model on the others, and average the deviance of
the held-out genotypes.
They draw the folds differently, so their errors are close but not
identical. fastmixture averages the same deviance, but holds out a fold of
the individuals rather than of the genotypes. The allele frequencies come
from the other individuals, but the ancestry of the held-out individuals is
estimated from their own genotypes, the same genotypes on which the error is
then computed. Its errors can be compared between values of K, but not with
those of the other two programs.

# How the benchmark was run

The benchmark is run with scripts in `vignettes/articles/code` (in the
source code of the package). The first prepares the data. The second runs
the programs from the command line: ADMIXTURE, fastmixture, and
`gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl with two more scripts, which `Rscript`
and `julia` run. The last runs `gt_radmix()` in an R session. The results are read here from
`vignettes/articles/data/admixture_benchmark`. Each run is done once, as the
full runs take long enough for the variation between repeated runs to be
small. The code shown below is taken from these scripts. Timings depend on
the machine (see [Machine and software](#machine-and-software)), but the
differences between the programs should be similar on other machines.

## The data

The data are those of the HGDP used in the benchmark of `tidypopgen`
(1043 individuals typed at about 650,000 loci), downloaded from Zenodo:

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
```

and prepared as recommended in the manual of ADMIXTURE. The steps are the
same as in the analyses of the HGDP with `tidygenclust`:

```{r filter, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r ld-clumping, eval = FALSE}
```

All the programs are run on this bed file. A small subset of it is also
saved, to check the scripts quickly (see
[Running the benchmark again](#running-the-benchmark-again)):

```{r quick-data, eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the programs from the command line

All the programs are run from the command line with the same settings:

```{bash cli-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program is run on `r cores_text` cores (with `-j` in ADMIXTURE,
`--threads` in fastmixture, `n_cores` in `gt_radmix()` and the number of
threads of Julia for OpenADMIXTURE.jl), with and without cross-validation
(with `--cv` in ADMIXTURE and fastmixture, and `crossval` in
`gt_radmix()`; OpenADMIXTURE.jl has none), with these functions:

```{bash cli-functions, eval = FALSE}
```

and the time, Q matrix, log-likelihood, cross-validation error and number of
iterations of each run are saved:

```{bash cli-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

From the command line, `gt_radmix()` is run by this R script (with
`Rscript`), which reads the same bed file into a `gen_tibble`, runs
`gt_radmix()`, and saves the result to an RDS file:

```{r r-cli, eval = FALSE}
```

and OpenADMIXTURE.jl by this Julia script (with `julia`), which runs it on
all the loci, without its selection of ancestry informative markers, with
its default settings, which are those of `gt_radmix()`:

```{r julia-run, eval = FALSE, lang = "julia"}
```

## Running gt_radmix() in an R session

`gt_radmix()` runs on a `gen_tibble`. Its parallel loops use OpenMP,
with `n_cores` threads. It only calls BLAS for small systems of K
equations, so BLAS is kept to a single thread:

```{r r-packages, eval = FALSE}
```

It is run with the same settings as the other programs:

```{r r-settings, eval = FALSE}
```

Each run reads the same bed file into a `gen_tibble`, runs
`gt_radmix()`, and saves the result to an RDS file:

```{r r-runs, eval = FALSE}
```

Each program stops when its own default convergence criterion is met.
ADMIXTURE stops when the log-likelihood increases by less than 1e-4 between
iterations. fastmixture checks every 5 iterations, and stops when the
log-likelihood, divided by the number of observed genotypes, has increased
by less than 1e-9. `gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl stop when the
relative change in the log-likelihood is less than 1e-7. The numbers of
iterations are not comparable either. An iteration of fastmixture is a pass
of accelerated EM updates, first over mini-batches of the loci. An
iteration of ADMIXTURE, `gt_radmix()` and OpenADMIXTURE.jl updates all the
parameters with block-wise Newton steps.

## From the results to the tables and plots

The results are read, and the Q matrices aligned and compared, with this
code:

```{r, ref.label = c("results_packages", "read_results", "align_q", "agreement"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the benchmark again

To run the benchmark again (e.g. after changing `tidygenclust`, or on
another machine), install `tidygenclust` with `R CMD INSTALL`, rather than
loading it with `devtools::load_all()`, which compiles its C++ code without
optimisation. Also install ADMIXTURE and fastmixture, e.g. in the conda
environment created by `tgc_tools_install()`, and OpenADMIXTURE.jl, in the
conda environment created (from the root of the package) by:

```sh
bash data-raw/radmix/setup_julia_env.sh
```

Then run, from `vignettes/articles`, on an otherwise idle machine with at
least `r max_cores` cores (the largest number of cores tested, set by
`cores` in the scripts):

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_data.R
conda activate ctidygenclust
bash code/admixture_benchmark_cli.sh
Rscript code/admixture_benchmark_radmix.R
```

The first script downloads and prepares the data in `data/hgdp`, which is
not part of the repository, and only needs to be run once. The other two
overwrite the results in `data/admixture_benchmark`; then render this
article again. With the argument `quick`, the last two scripts run
everything on the small subset of the data, to check them in less time.
They then save their results in `data/admixture_benchmark_quick`, which this
article can be rendered on with:

```r
rmarkdown::render(
  "admixture_benchmark.Rmd",
  params = list(results_dir = "data/admixture_benchmark_quick")
)
```
